cities.name: Austin
found: City sales are slowing. October closings were down 14.6% on the year, pending sales down 12.6%, new listings down 19.4% (Unlock MLS, Austin's MLS).
The city median price fell from $570,958 in September to $550,000 in October, flat on the year. It covers all home types, so part of the drop may be mix.
Supply is rising: 5.7 months of inventory in October, up from 5.4. The metro median was down 6.9% on the year in October.
Builders discount mainly through financing incentives, which may not show up in recorded prices (old, weak source).
cities.call: Analyst: −0.10 pp, low confidence. Director cut it to 0, because the model already shades Austin down 0.12 pp through the metro-gap term, so it would count twice.
cities.gaps: No single-family-only city figures; Redfin and Case-Shiller not checked.

cities.name: Chicago
found: No September or October city data could be read (Illinois Realtors PDFs unreadable, Axios blocked).
The August city median was up 8.0% on the year, down from 13.3% in July, so growth is slowing. It includes condos.
Redfin: September pending sales down 5.8% on the year; a balanced market. No city reassessment in 2026.
Zillow's Chicago index has been rising 0.8–0.9% a month, about twice its 5.2% yearly pace, so the analyst expects it to fade.
cities.call: Analyst: −0.20 pp, low confidence, slightly wider on the downside. Director cut it to 0: fading momentum is already in the model, and the metro-gap term already adds −0.07 pp.
cities.gaps: No single-family or mid-tier data; every median seen mixes in condos.

cities.name: Dallas
found: Only metro-level, mostly blog-quality data. Dallas–Fort Worth September median about $379,990, down 1.6% on the year; sales down about 7%.
Builders are cutting prices, and new builds are 31% of listings, which leans down.
The October MetroTex report is not out yet.
cities.call: Analyst: 0 (at most −0.05 pp), low confidence. Director: 0.

cities.name: Hoboken
found: No September or October sales data from any source.
Very thin market: about 32 single-family sales in 12 months, so a handful of closings moves the index. Recent months: +0.68%, +0.64%, +0.11%.
The city passed a large tax increase in its 2026 budget.
cities.call: Analyst: 0, wider spread. Director: 0; the wider spread is recorded but not applied.
cities.gaps: Nothing local can be observed; Zillow's revisions dominate.

cities.name: Jersey City
found: Confirmed: a 15% municipal tax-rate increase, about $51 a month for the average home, on Q3 2026 bills.
No single-family sales data for August to October. The only October figures are broker and aggregator pages that conflict with each other.
Single-family homes are a small slice of a mostly-condo city, so the index rests on few sales.
Index trend is barely positive: +0.16% in August, +0.12% in September.
cities.call: Analyst: 0 (at most −0.05 pp), wider spread. Director: 0; spread recorded, not applied.
cities.gaps: The main tax source is behind a sign-in; Hudson County MLS and Zillow pages were unreadable.

cities.name: Los Angeles
found: California Realtors September data: prices flat to slightly up, sales weaker.
The only LA-specific September numbers ($855k metro, $994,670 county) come from a weak aggregator site.
Nothing city-level was found that would bend the near-flat trend (September +0.12%).
cities.gaps: No primary city-of-LA single-family data for September or October.

cities.name: Miami
found: Miami-Dade single-family, September (Miami Realtors): median $692,000, up 4.1% on the year; closed sales down 4.7%; new pending sales down 11.6%; listings down 16.6%; 5.1 months of supply against 6.5 a year ago.
Prices are firm and volume is soft; for November the two roughly offset. Recent index moves: +0.35%, +0.44%.
All of this is county-level, not City of Miami. The October report comes out 2026-11-16.

cities.name: New York
found: No 1–3 family closed-price data for the outer boroughs for September or October.
Third-quarter borough figures are mixed: Brooklyn house contracts up 8%, Queens house closings up 8.7%, Queens house median down.
Momentum is steady: the index rose 0.40% in August and 0.39% in September.
cities.gaps: No October price data published yet.

Prop TE is passing but not yet certified.
No September or October sales report could be read (Redfin blocked).
The mix of lots, rebuilds and surviving homes in Zillow's sample can't be seen from outside.
cities.call: Analyst: 0, wider spread. Director: 0; spread recorded, not applied.

cities.name: Palo Alto
found: The only fresh data is a broker page covering the quarter to October 31: 28 single-family sales, median $3.715M, selling at 105% of list price, 9 median days on market. A hot market.
Santa Clara County median down 4.0% on the year in September (secondary source, unverified).
The index jumped 1.2% in August and 1.5% in September. With about 400 sales a year, a few $8M+ sales can drive it.
cities.call: Analyst: −0.20 pp as a judgment haircut on extending the jump, wider spread. Director cut it to 0: the model already takes 0.164 pp off through the metro-gap term, and the direct evidence points up. A wider spread is the right response; recorded, not applied.
cities.gaps: The Aug–Sep jump couldn't be checked against actual closings.

cities.name: Philadelphia
found: City prices are up about 4.6% on the year, while September closed sales fell 3% and days on market rose by 4.
Redfin's metro index rose 1.9% in September, the most of 50 metros (search snippet, unverified).
The 2027 property reassessment takes effect 2027-01-01; its size is unknown and it is unlikely to reach Zillow by November.
The index moves very little: +0.06%, +0.11% in recent months.
cities.gaps: October Bright MLS report not yet out; evidence is mostly search snippets.

cities.name: Phoenix
found: City of Phoenix single-family median down 3.5% on the year in September; pending sales down 37.3%.
Metro median down 1.5% on the year in October; October contracts down 13.5%; supply rising to 4.3 months.
The index decline is slowing: −0.22% in July, −0.07% in August, −0.03% in September.
cities.call: Analyst: −0.05 pp, slightly wider. Director cut it to 0: inside noise, and the price decline is already in the index.

cities.name: San Diego
found: Only county-level September data: sales down 12.2% on the year and 6% on the month; average price fell from $1.09M to $1.05M (average, all home types, so weak).
Momentum is about +0.1% a month, and nothing found breaks it.

A few hundred single-family sales a year, so mix and Zillow's revisions can dominate.
Measure ULA (LA's mansion tax) does not apply in Santa Monica.
cities.call: Analyst: 0, wider spread. Director: 0; spread recorded, not applied.

cities.name: Seattle
found: NWMLS October: King County single-family median $925,000, down 7.2% on the year; active listings up 32.8%.
Zillow's Seattle index was only down 1.6% on the year at August, so it may still have catching down to do.
September index move was −0.11%. The county median was about $949,975 in September, so the October dip is partly seasonal and mix.
cities.call: Analyst: −0.10 pp, low confidence. Director kept −0.05 pp, the only adjustment that survived: verified primary source, single-family, and no double count with the model.
cities.gaps: County-level, not city; no city month-on-month figures.
